detailZh: 马克斯·维斯塔潘透露红牛在巴库F1排位赛中真正出了什么问题
维斯塔潘表示，排位赛期间内燃机运转不正常，随后引发了更多问题。这位红牛车手补充说，如果更换发动机，他不会受到发车位处罚
在最后一次练习赛中做出最快圈速并对升级感到满意之后，维斯塔潘本希望在巴库带来一个惊喜，但发动机问题打乱了计划
起初，这看起来似乎与能量输出问题有关，也就是动力单元电气部分的问题，但在巴库围场里对（规模很小的）荷兰媒体小组讲话时，维斯塔潘澄清了实际情况。
"从第一节排位赛开始，我就遇到了引擎的问题，这意味着比起我的队友，我至少损失了半秒。而且情况越来越糟。在第二节和第三节排位赛中简直是一场灾难，所以我认为我们显然在引擎方面存在问题。"
当Motorsport.com提问时，维斯塔潘澄清说，这个问题最初并非出在能量输出上——尽管看起来可能是——而是出在内燃机上。
"不，不是电气系统的问题。在第一节排位赛中，我们立刻发现了问题。当然，那时候你会想：‘这可能是什么呢？是引擎太冷了，还是其实太热了？’这些都有可能，因为如今这一切都非常敏感。但后来我们清楚了，内燃机确实出了问题。情况越来越糟，到了第三节排位赛，那台引擎已经完全无法正常工作了。"
最初的问题如何导致了后续的挫折
内燃机的这个问题随后引发了诸多其他故障，导致维斯塔潘在周五下午从一个问题陷入另一个问题。
"最高速度变得越来越低。在第三节排位赛的第二圈，我的电池也没法充电，但这显然是因为内燃机出了问题。它造成了很多失火和许多其他问题，完全把系统搞乱了。"
后者在车载镜头中清晰可见。在15号弯和16号弯之间，维斯塔潘的头突然向前一冲，而这段通常应该是全油门通过的路段。
"对，因为我的电池在那里断电了",这位荷兰车手解释道。"因为你在直道上太慢，你自然会在出弯时使用更多电池来试图弥补。结果在某些地方就进入了超级削波（super clipping）状态，而那种削波是相当剧烈的。"
"整套系统完全混乱了。因为速度慢，你在直道上花的时间更长，结果电池消耗也更多。这和本田的情况一样，你也能看到他们比其他所有人都更容易出现电量耗尽（clip）的情况，因为他们必须在直道上更长时间地保持全油门。"
除了引擎本身的问题之外，这也打乱了练习计划。维斯塔潘不得不放弃他的第二个飞驰圈——或者说本应是飞驰圈的一圈——而这又对接下来的整节排位赛产生了影响。
"我不得不放弃那一圈，但这样一来轮胎温度就损失了很多，而这在这里其实非常重要。你能看到所有人都在不停地推进、继续左右摆动轮胎（weave）来保温"，维斯塔潘说，并指出排位赛第三节（Q3）几乎所有人都只跑了一个长距离单圈——这与正常的第三节排位赛不同。
只有迈凯伦选择进了维修通道，但维斯塔潘继续说道："你可以看到这对他们来说其实也不算成功，所以我们干脆继续跑。"
“但如果你不得不放弃一个单圈，那么你在最后一个单圈时轮胎温度就不合适了。而且发动机基本上快要报废了，然后在我最后一圈还出现了黄旗”，他说道，指的是涉及兰多·诺里斯的那次事件。“所以在那个弯角，我至少损失了两个十分之二秒。”
维斯塔潘更换了发动机，但不会受到发车罚退？
红牛目前仍在进一步调查发动机问题，但维斯塔潘的说法表明，他周六的正赛很可能不会使用同一台内燃机（ICE）。不过，这位四届世界冠军立即明确表示，这样的发动机更换不会导致发车罚退。
“嗯，如果仍然存在疑问，我们就必须更换发动机。但我们的发动机储备库里还有另一台可用的发动机。”
不过，当本网站向这位红牛车手提问时，他确认今年晚些时候将接受一次发车处罚。“是的，在某个阶段肯定会有一次处罚。”
理论上，巴库似乎是个接受处罚的绝佳地点，因为在那里看起来有机会超车，但维斯塔潘对此提出了不同看法。
“问题在于，所有人都会在长直道上把电池电量完全耗尽。所以你根本没法利用电池去超车，因为从100%用到0%对每个人来说都是一样的。”
这意味着维斯塔潘将保留他第八位的发车位置，并且在周六依然会把目标放在登上领奖台上，尽管他认为如果没有这次处罚，自己本可以从前排发车。
“这显然非常令人遗憾，因为这一周进展一直很顺利。也许我本来无法追上拉塞尔的圈速，但第一名和第二名之间差距这么大，我们肯定能排在他们两人之间。”
detailEn: Max Verstappen reveals what really went wrong for Red Bull in Baku F1 qualifying

Verstappen says the internal combustion engine was not working properly during qualifying, which then led to further problems. The Red Bull driver adds that he will not receive a grid penalty in the event of an engine change
After setting the fastest time in final practice and feeling good about the upgrades, Verstappen hoped to pull off a surprise in Baku, but an engine problem threw a spanner in the works.

Initially, it appeared to be related to deployment issues and therefore problems on the electrical side of the power unit, but speaking to the (very small) group of Dutch media in the Baku paddock, Verstappen clarified what was actually going on.

"Throughout qualifying, already from Q1, I had a problem with the engine, which meant I was losing at least half a second compared to my team-mate. And it only got worse. In Q2 and Q3 it was a complete disaster, so I think we clearly have a problem with the engine."
When asked by Motorsport.com, Verstappen clarified that the problem was initially not about deployment – as it perhaps seemed – but rather the internal combustion engine.

"No, not on the electrical side. In Q1, we immediately saw a problem. Of course, at that point you still think, ‘What could it be? Is the engine too cold or actually too hot?’ All of that is possible, because it is all very sensitive nowadays. But later it became clear that we really did have a problem with the ICE. It only got worse and in Q3 that engine was no longer working properly at all."
How the initial issue led to further setbacks
That problem with the combustion engine subsequently caused numerous other issues, leaving Verstappen going from one problem to another on Friday afternoon.

"The top speed just became less and less. On that second lap in Q3, my battery wasn’t charging either, but that was obviously because the combustion engine had a problem. That causes a lot of misfires and a lot of other problems, and it confuses the system completely."
The latter was clearly visible in the onboard footage. Between Turns 15 and 16, Verstappen’s head suddenly jolted forward, whereas this would normally be a straightforward flat-out section.

"Yeah, because my battery switched off there", the Dutchman explained. "Because you’re so slow on the straights, you obviously use more battery coming out of the corners to try to compensate for that. As a result, you go into super clipping in some places, and that clip is quite aggressive.

"The whole system was just confused. You spend longer on a straight because you’re going slowly and as a result you use more battery. That’s the same as what happens with Honda, you also see them clipping a lot more than everyone else because they have to spend longer at full throttle on the straights."

Besides the engine problems themselves, this also disrupted the run plan. Verstappen had to abort his second flying lap – or what should have been a flying lap – which in turn had consequences for the remainder of the session.

"I had to abort that lap, but then you lose so much tyre temperature, which is actually very important around here. You could see everyone pushing all the time and continuing to weave", Verstappen said, pointing out that almost everyone in Q3 completed just one long run – unlike in a normal Q3 session.
Only McLaren opted for a visit to the pitlane, but Verstappen continued: "You can see that it wasn’t really a success for them either, so we just kept going.

"But if you have to abort a lap, then you don’t have the right tyre temperature for the very last lap. And the engine is basically breaking down, and then there was a yellow flag on my final lap as well”, he said, referring to the moment involving Lando Norris. “So I had to leave at least two tenths on the table in that corner."
An engine change, but no grid penalty for Verstappen?

Red Bull is currently investigating the engine problem further, but Verstappen’s story makes it seem unlikely that he will start Saturday’s race with the same ICE. However, the four-time world champion immediately makes clear that such an engine change will not result in a grid penalty.
"Well, if there are still question marks, we have to replace the engine. But we still have another engine available in the pool."
A grid penalty will follow later in the year, however, the Red Bull driver confirmed when asked by this website. "Yeah, there definitely has to be a penalty at some point."
In theory, Baku appeared to be quite a good place to take one, as overtaking seems possible, but Verstappen puts that into perspective.
"The problem is that everyone completely drains the battery on the long straight. So you can’t really use the battery to overtake someone, because going from 100 to zero is the same for everyone."
It means Verstappen retains his eighth starting position and will still be aiming for the podium on Saturday, although he believes he could otherwise have started from the front row.

"It’s obviously a real shame, because it had been going well this week. Maybe I wouldn’t have matched George’s time, but there’s such a big gap between P1 and P2, we definitely would have been somewhere in between."

Lewis Hamilton expressed frustration with Ferrari's approach to Q3 after qualifying sixth for the Azerbaijan Grand Prix, saying "they changed the plan".

Hamilton questioned why the team completed only one run of multiple laps at the end of the final knockout stage rather than go out earlier for initial laps, as Mercedes, McLaren and Red Bull with Max Verstappen had done.

The seven-time world champion said his final laps were compromised by having no 'tow' from a car in front to aid straight-line speed down Baku's long main straight. Team-mate Charles Leclerc did have a tow, from Hamilton, by dint of the fact it was the Monegasque's turn to go out second in final qualifying.

"Instead of doing two runs we ended up waiting and then because I was ahead of Charles, I had nobody ahead of me on a tow so that was worth quite a chunk in itself.
"But, either way, we couldn't compete with the Mercedes. They are just outright so much quicker on the straights than us. They did a great job."
Three of the five cars in front of Hamilton on the grid - Russell and McLaren duo Oscar Piastri and Lando Norris - for Saturday's race at 1pm run Mercedes engines.
"I think it's going to be hard to overtake a Mercedes tomorrow," added Hamilton.
"Keeping up with a Mercedes engine on the straight will be tough but I'll give it everything I've got."
Sky Sports F1's Karun Chandhok is joined by George Russell to watch back his pole-setting lap for the Azerbaijan GP.
Speaking in Ferrari's post-qualifying press release, team principal Frederic Vasseur said: "We made some significant changes to the set-up and to our approach, and they paid off today.
"George has been very strong since the first lap of FP1, but Charles did a good job to put the car on the front row.

"On Lewis' side, it was difficult to get a tow because the different run plans made it complicated to synchronise with the other cars. He also brushed the wall on his first lap in Q3, which compromised that attempt, but he recovered well to finish sixth despite not having a tow on his final lap."
'We know we have a good race car' - Leclerc hopes for strong Saturday race

Leclerc, who claimed Ferrari's first front-row since the Hungarian Grand Prix in July, was pleased with his lap but admitted the gap to Russell was "a lot more than what we expected" despite a challenging Thursday.
"Honestly, it was quite a good lap," he added. "Lewis was three-four seconds, I think, in front, and I managed to do a good lap at the end.
"But when I see the gap to George, maybe the lap wasn't good enough."
Craig Slater breaks down the Azerbaijan Grand Prix, including why the race takes place on a Saturday, while doing his best Craig David impression!
But Leclerc offered a more optimistic assessment of what he could potentially do from the front row after encouraging long-run pace in practice.
"We'll try, and we'll do our best," said Leclerc. "Whether that'll be enough, only time will tell.
"But we know that we have a good race car, more often than not better in the race than in qualifying, and I hope that it will be the case again this weekend."
Vasseur, whose team have claimed no podium finishes in the last four races, added: "Tyre degradation is expected to be very low, which could make track position particularly important.
"We are in a position to score good points with both cars, even if Baku is always unpredictable."

items.originalTitle: Winners and losers from F1 Azerbaijan GP qualifying
items.summaryEn: The Race reviews the winners and losers from Azerbaijan Grand Prix qualifying: Russell took pole by a huge 0.837s margin, Antonelli hit the wall and qualified only 16th, Verstappen was hampered by an engine issue, while Hadjar, Sainz and Gasly had mixed fortunes.
detailZh: 作为头条数据，巴库街道赛道上迄今最大的杆位优势似乎表明阿塞拜疆大奖赛排位赛可能缺乏一些锋芒。
现实却截然不同——不仅仅是因为两位梅赛德斯车手命运迥异。
以下是我们选出的周五赢家与输家：
考虑到梅赛德斯本周末至今的表现，即使安东内利的周四被证明多么受影响，这仍然（相对而言）是唾手可得的18分。
这仍然是一个可能的结果，但在第一节排位赛中“不必要地”撞上1号弯内侧护墙后，现在肯定会更难。
“与上一圈相比，我遇到了更大的逆风，所以前部抓地力强得多，我在大致相同的位置入弯，但显然赛车转得更多，我蹭到了墙，”安东内利解释道。
口袋里已有81分，他承受得起——但本周末没有必要‘花掉’其中一部分优势。也许他不会——但就发车位和现在需要完成的超车而言，他已经把自己置于一个有点危险的境地。——Valentin Khorounzhiy
甚至在领跑积分榜的安东内利蹭到1号弯墙之前，拉塞尔就已经状态惊人。没有队友竞争，这变成了以0.837秒的压倒性优势夺得杆位。
拉塞尔称自己从周末开始就感觉“连接”得很好，而被他称为“最大威胁”的维斯塔潘受到黄旗和日益严重的引擎问题阻碍，拉塞尔则始终看起来有望夺得杆位。
虽然要重燃他黯淡的争冠希望，远不止一个杆位、甚至周六一场胜利，但这是拉塞尔所说的提升表现的“上升周期”中的重要一步。——Edd Straw
维斯塔潘认为由于引擎/动力相关问题，他比伊萨克·哈贾尔慢了半秒——而维斯塔潘在Q3中落后哈贾尔多少？0.581秒。
好吧，你会预期维斯塔潘（他在FP3中排名第一）在消除半秒差距后能击败哈贾尔，尤其是在哈贾尔因伤缺席三场比赛之后，而且如果他没有在最后一圈遇到黄旗，他可能仍然做到了。
在那之前的第二圈，他的电池在冲向终点线的过程中没有达到100%，所以又失去了一次机会。再加上赛车前部触底导致刹车困难，这意味着原本看起来很有希望的一天变成了维斯塔潘的噩梦。——Jack Benyon
哈贾尔在迄今为止的F1生涯中一直是个半空杯心态的车手，他强调如果保持连续性而不是受伤，他“肯定”会在这里进入头排——结果他以0.141秒之差错过。
“没什么特别的，”他补充道。但尽管2027年的合同已经到手，在利亚姆·劳森作为替补连续三场展现出令人印象深刻的勤恳速度之后，现在提醒大家哈贾尔今年拥有真正的速度，当然不是坏时机。
他确实承认，他很高兴自己在本周末如此从容地进入状态，而这条赛道随时可能让你栽跟头。
“我告诉自己，绝对不能碰墙或任何东西。对于复出来说，冒很多风险没有意义。所以整个周末在那个非常狭窄的路段，我实际上开得有点低于极限——我想我在Q3只是迈出了自然的一步。”——VK
两辆大幅升级的奥迪在练习赛中并未给人留下深刻印象——但即便如此，双车Q1出局看起来也像是个异常。
加布里埃尔·博托莱托坚称，这不仅仅是动力单元的问题。
“像蒙扎这样的赛道，我们几乎进了Q3，而且那里的直道比这里多。所以我认为我们需要理解的是更大的问题，”他说。
“我认为[周末早些时候]更好，但我们始终处于Q1出局的边缘。
“整个周末我们都没有抓地力。如果没有抓地力，你就无法在弯道中开快。如果开不快，就做不出圈速。就这么简单，其他车队在Q1出局时可能也会这么说。”
队友尼科·霍肯伯格相对而言更乐观，他认为自己Q1出局“主要是由于情况”，具体来说是黄旗和失去尾流。他和博托莱托都没有暗示升级出了问题——但显然这对巴库来说并非改变格局的因素。——VK
塞恩斯将威廉姆斯本赛季首次带入Q3，其重大升级在首秀中表现出色——尽管塞恩斯觉得这个结果超出了赛车实力。
亚历克斯·阿尔本与塞恩斯一同进入Q2，威廉姆斯自7月英国大奖赛以来首次双车逃离Q1，这证明FW48在巴库是更具竞争力的猛兽。
但塞恩斯（他仍面临黄旗调查）觉得他的第九名是威廉姆斯精准把握轮胎使用和运行计划，以及他自己“几圈极限驾驶”的结果，最终排名略高于赛车纯粹速度所能达到的位置。
他形容赛车“感觉没有不同，只是更快了”，因为它更轻且下压力稍大——但为实现这一点所做的工作立即得到了回报。
塞恩斯承认，在经历了在中游车队下游苦苦挣扎的一年后，取得一个引人注目的成绩对他个人来说感觉相当不错——并形容实现这一成绩的圈速是“本赛季压力最大的”，因为在阵风天气和低抓地力赛道上，穿越第二赛段的弯道充满挑战。
那么，遗憾的是，这些出色工作的大部分因未在黄旗下减速而被罚退五位发车而付诸东流。——Scott Mitchell-Malm
前述哈贾尔在Q2的锁死（右前轮，让他冲入15号弯逃生路）对他自己的排位赛没有实际影响——但却加剧了另一位法国车手的痛苦。
奥康在Q2最后一圈前对队友奥利·贝尔曼拥有0.3秒优势，但回到赛道后的第一次尝试未能匹配贝尔曼——他形容自己受到“一阵风”的影响，似乎让他冲上16号弯外侧路肩。
“然后我在到达15号弯前又做出了同样的圈速。我不知道是谁冲出去了[哈贾尔]，但我不得不在出弯时减速，以确保我不会受到任何处罚，”他发泄道。
“我做出了完全相同的圈速。所以是的，我损失了，大概三四成？难以置信。你知道，我简直无语。不同的比赛周末，同样的破事。总是有什么事情发生在我这边，要么是赛车，要么是别的什么，现在是黄旗、安全车，随便什么。
“但我不该承受目前压在我身上的所有这些破事。所以我不知道，我可能需要好好洗个澡。”——VK
阿尔派充分利用安东内利的缺席，让两辆赛车都进入Q3——对于任何中游车队来说，当顶级车队通常占据前十名中的八个位置时，这都是美好的一天。
皮埃尔·加斯利设法击败了马克斯·维斯塔潘——虽然有维斯塔潘动力问题的前提，但仍然令人印象深刻——他的看法是“平衡很好，赛车很好，相当轻松地进入Q3”。
弗朗哥·科拉平托则更为挣扎，他因轮胎平斑冲入15号弯缓冲区，也影响了加斯利最后一圈飞驰圈。加斯利认为如果没有那次事故，第六名的刘易斯·汉密尔顿也是可以挑战的。
Q3有些混乱，但无关紧要，加斯利有信心将其他‘中游’车手甩在身后。——JB
机会就在那里，但用佩雷斯的话说，凯迪拉克“需要一切顺利”才能首次进入Q2。
佩雷斯表示，凯迪拉克在如何与队友瓦尔特利·博塔斯准备圈速方面采用了“错误的计划”。当原本要提供尾流的博塔斯被叫去称重时，情况进一步恶化。
detailEn: As a headline statistic, the biggest pole position margin yet around the streets of Baku points to an Azerbaijan Grand Prix qualifying session that might've lacked a bit of edge.
The reality was very different - and not just because of the contrasting fortunes of the two Mercedes drivers.
Here's our pick of winners and losers from Friday:
Given Mercedes' form so far this weekend, even with how compromised Antonelli's Thursday had proven this was still an easy (relatively speaking) 18 points just begging to be collected.
That's still a plausible outcome, but it sure will be harder now after an "unnecessary" impact with the inside barrier at Turn 1 during the opening segment.

"I had a lot more headwind compared to the lap before, so the front just was much stronger, and I turned in roughly in the same spot, but obviously the car turned more and I clipped the wall," Antonelli explained.

With 81 points in the pocket he can afford it - but there's no need to 'spend' a chunk of that margin this weekend. And maybe he won't - but he's put himself in a bit of a danger zone, in terms of grid position and the overtaking he will now need to do. - Valentin Khorounzhiy

Even before runaway championship leader Antonelli clipped the Turn 1 wall, Russell had been in formidable form. Without his team-mate for competition, that turned into pole position by a crushing margin of 0.837s.

Russell described himself as feeling "hooked up" from the start of the weekend, and while Max Verstappen, who he described as "the biggest threat", was hindered by yellow flags and a worsening engine issue, Russell always looked on target for pole position.

While it will take far more than one pole position, or even a victory on Saturday, to reignite his faded title chances, it's an important step in what Russell calls the "upward cycle" of improving his performances. - Edd Straw
Max Verstappen reckoned he was losing half a second to Isack Hadjar because of an engine/power-related problem - and what was Verstappen's deficit to Hadjar in Q3? 0.581s.

OK, you'd expect Verstappen (who topped FP3) to beat Hadjar with the half-second deficit removed, especially after Hadjar's three-race injury lay-off, and he might still have done had he not caught a yellow flag on his final run.

On his second run prior to that, his battery didn't go to 100% for the run to the finish line, so that was another chance lost. Combined with the car's front-bottoming, which caused brake struggles, that meant a day that looked so promising turned into a nightmare for Verstappen. - Jack Benyon
Ever a glass-half-empty driver in his time in F1 so far, Hadjar emphasised that with continuity instead of injury he would've "definitely" been on the front row here - instead missing out by 0.141s.

"Nothing outstanding," he added. But while a 2027 deal is already in his pocket it's certainly not a bad time to remind everyone, after three rounds of impressively workmanlike stand-in pace from Liam Lawson, that Hadjar has had serious speed this year.
And he did admit he has been happy about how he's eased himself into this weekend, at a track that is just waiting to catch you out.

"I told myself it's mandatory not to touch the wall or anything. For a comeback, there's no point taking a lot of risks. So I was really driving a bit under the limit the whole weekend in that very tight section - I think I just did that natural step in Q3." - VK
The two heavily-upgraded Audis had not impressed very much in practice - but even so, the double Q1 exit looks like an aberration.
It's not just the power unit, Gabriel Bortoleto insisted.
"There were tracks like Monza where we were almost in Q3 and there are more straights than here. So I think it's something bigger that we need to understand," he said.
"I think it was better [earlier in the weekend], but still we were always on the edge of going out in Q1.

"The whole weekend we had no grip. If you don't have grip, you cannot go fast in the corners. If you don't go fast, you don't make a laptime. It's simple as that, and it's what other teams, when they go out in Q1, they probably say."

Team-mate Nico Hulkenberg was more cheery, in relative terms, arguing his Q1 exit was "mostly because of circumstances", specifically a yellow flag and a lost tow. And neither he nor Bortoleto is suggesting the upgrade is misfiring - but certainly it's proving no game changer for Baku. - VK
Sainz put Williams into Q3 for the first time this year as its significant car upgrade excelled on debut - although Sainz felt the result was an overachievement.
Alex Albon joined Sainz in Q2 as Williams escaped Q1 with both cars for the first time since July's British GP, which serves as evidence the FW48 is a more competitive beast in Baku.

But Sainz (who does still face a yellow flag investigation) felt his ninth place was a result of Williams nailing its tyre usage and run plan, and "some serious laps on the limit" from himself, to end up a little higher than it would be on pace alone.
He described the car as no different "in feel, just quicker" because it's lighter and has a bit more downforce - but the work done to achieve that has been immediately rewarded.

Sainz admitted that getting a noticeable result felt pretty good for him, too, after a year spent toiling further down the midfield - and described the laps to achieve that as "the highest stress of the season" because of the challenge threading through the twists of sector two on a gusty day and low-grip track.
What a shame, then, that a good deal of that good work was undone by a five-place grid drop for failing to slow for yellow flags. - Scott Mitchell-Malm

That aforementioned Hadjar lock-up in Q2 (on the right front, sending him into the Turn 15 escape road) had no real impact on his own qualifying - but did compound the misery of another French driver.

Ocon had three tenths in hand over team-mate Ollie Bearman coming into their final run in Q2, but couldn't match Bearman with his first effort after returning to the track - compromised by what he described as a "gust of wind", which seemingly sent him onto the outside kerb at Turn 16.

"And then I did the same laptime, again, [before] arriving to Turn 15. I don't know who went off [Hadjar], but I had to back off on the exit to make sure that I was not going to get any penalty," he vented.

"I did exactly the same laptime. So yeah, I lost, what, three-four tenths? Unbelievable. You know, I just have no words. It's different race weekend, same s**t. It's always something going on, on my side, if it's either the car, if it's something else, now yellow flag, safety cars, whatever.
"But I don't deserve all the s**t that I have on my back at the moment. So I don't know, I might need to take a good shower." - VK
Alpine took full advantage of Antonelli's absence to get both cars into Q3 - a good day for any midfield team when the top teams usually hog eight of the 10 spots at the top of the order.
Pierre Gasly managed to beat Max Verstappen - caveated by Verstappen's power issue, but still impressive - with his take being "great balance, great car, managed to get to Q3 pretty comfortably".

Franco Colapinto had more of a struggle, and his off into the Turn 15 run-off, blamed on a flatspot, also cost Gasly on his final flying lap. Gasly reckoned sixth-place qualifier Lewis Hamilton was also there for the taking without that.
A scruffy Q3, but it didn't matter, and Gasly's confident of keeping the rest of the 'midfield' behind. - JB
The opportunity was there but, in the words of Perez, Cadillac "needed everything to go our way" to bag its first Q2 appearance.

Perez said Cadillac had the "wrong programme" in terms of how he and team-mate Valtteri Bottas prepared their laps. That went further awry when Bottas, who was due to provide the tow, was called to the weighbridge.

梅赛德斯在这条赛道上的实力体现在安东内利的队友——也是他最接近的争冠对手——乔治·拉塞尔以超过0.8秒的优势击败法拉利的查尔斯·勒克莱尔夺得杆位。
梅赛德斯的安东内利在阿塞拜疆大奖赛因一次“不必要”的撞车提前结束排位赛后感到沮丧
当被问及是否因为第一弯抓地力比他预想的更多而措手不及时，安东内利告诉天空体育 F1：“是的，当然。抓地力一圈比一圈提升得很快。”
“突然我转向时，前部抓地力比上一圈多得多，然后我碰到了墙。”
“所以，是我的失误。非常不必要。说实话，我对此非常恼火，明天会努力做得更好。”
“过去的基米”的“不可思议的失误”
前世界冠军雅克·维伦纽夫将这一事件描述为“不可思议的失误”。
“这不是一英寸的问题，而是很多，”天空体育 F1的维伦纽夫说。“不可思议的失误，而且他是在队友独一档的周末犯下这个错误。”
“这个时机不太好，但按照现行规则，他们更容易从后方追回来。”
2026年阿塞拜疆大奖赛排位赛集锦
三届W系列赛冠军杰米·查德威克表示，这次撞车让她想起“过去的基米”，指的是这位20岁车手在F1首个赛季表现不稳定，曾引发人们对他能否兑现一代天才声誉的重大质疑。
天空体育 F1的查德威克说：“我说这很不寻常，我们经常看到基米开车的方式就是只有一个挡位。全速前进。全力以赴。”
“去年我们看到这带来了失误和撞车，今年我们在他身上基本没看到这种情况。感觉有点像过去的基米，就是那种只有一个挡位，而他其实并不需要那样做。”
“话虽如此，在这样的赛道上，我们知道很容易犯这种错误。但你开的是一辆在这条赛道上明显独一档的梅赛德斯，Q1第一圈，你不需要冒那么大风险。”
“只是第一弯的抓地力让他措手不及。他转向时，进入排位赛，赛车总是比FP3时更有活力一些，这让他措手不及。”
拉塞尔“不能排除”安东内利争胜
周六的比赛距离安东内利在意大利大奖赛的惊艳胜利仅三周，那场比赛他从第19位发车，最终赢下主场之战。
在蒙扎从第二位发车并一度领先、随后被安东内利超越的拉塞尔，对队友在巴库从后方发车可能构成的威胁保持警惕。
“显然，你不能排除基米，”拉塞尔说。“他在蒙扎从第19位发车，现在他在第16位，所以这次他应该能提前几圈领跑。”
拉塞尔被问及是否认为安东内利在接近首个冠军时出现“紧张”，但他指出，即使在夺冠赛季，车手也往往会犯错。
天空体育 F1的卡伦·钱多克与乔治·拉塞尔一起回看他在阿塞拜疆大奖赛的杆位圈
这位英国人更愿意专注于自己在巴库迄今的强劲表现，即使在Q1撞车之前，他似乎也对比安东内利占据优势。
“我想不起来他本赛季犯过多少错误，”拉塞尔说。“我们今天这边的表现很棒，但他整个赛季都无懈可击。”
“当你回顾每一个冠军赛季，即使是最终获胜者，过程中也会有失误。”
“我仍然继续相信、继续战斗，直到不再可能为止，但我没有感到任何压力。现在每次坐进车里我都感到兴奋，纯粹是因为我对自己更有信心。”
“当这种信心开始建立时，就像是一个向上的循环。反过来，当你处于被动时，你开始失去信心，然后你开始更多地挑战极限，那正是失误发生的时候。”
detailEn: Kimi Antonelli 'very mad' about Azerbaijan GP qualifying crash as George Russell refuses to discount team-mate from battle for win

Kimi Antonelli crashed in the first part of qualifying in Azerbaijan, leaving him 16th on the grid; George Russell exhibited Mercedes' strong pace by taking pole; watch the Azerbaijan GP on Saturday at 12pm with build-up from 10.30am, live on Sky Sports F1 and Main Event
Kimi Antonelli hits the wall during qualifying at the Azerbaijan GP
World championship leader Kimi Antonelli said he was "very mad" about making an "unnecessary" qualifying error that left him starting the Azerbaijan Grand Prix from 16th on the grid.
The 81-point lead established by Antonelli at the top of the standings with nine races remaining has put him in a position where merely solid results will see the Italian to a maiden title.

For that reason, along with the imperious form he has shown throughout the season so far, it came as a major surprise when Antonelli clipped the wall at the first corner during Q1 in Baku, especially given Mercedes were showing strong pace that should have enabled him to cruise through to Q3 at a canter.

The Silver Arrows' strength at the circuit was evidenced in Antonelli's team-mate - and nearest title challenger - George Russell beating Ferrari's Charles Leclerc to pole by more than eight tenths of a second.
Mercedes' Antonelli was left frustrated after an 'unnecessary' crash which ended his qualifying early at the Azerbaijan GP
Asked whether he had been caught out by there being more grip than he expected at the first corner, Antonelli told Sky Sports F1: "Yeah, for sure. The grip was coming up very quickly lap by lap.
"Suddenly I turned in and had a lot more front end compared to the lap before and I touched the wall.
"So, mistake from my side. Very unnecessary. To be fair, I'm very mad about it and will try to do better tomorrow."
'An incredible mistake' from 'the Kimi of old'
Former world champion Jacques Villeneuve described the incident as "an incredible mistake".
"It's not an inch, it's a lot," Sky Sports F1's Villeneuve said. "An incredible mistake and he does it on a weekend where his team-mate is in a league of his own.
"Not the best of time for that, but with the current rules they facilitate getting back through the field."

Three-time W series champion Jamie Chadwick said the crash reminded her of "Kimi of old", a reference to the 20-year-old's inconsistent debut campaign in F1, which raised major doubts over whether he could live up to his billing as a generational talent.
Sky Sports F1's Chadwick said: "I say it's uncharacteristic, it's kind of the way we see Kimi drive a lot of the time is that there's one gear. It's all in. It's all everything.

"Last year we saw that come with mistakes and crashes, this year we have not really seen that of him. It has felt a bit like Kimi of old in a way and it was like that one gear and he just didn't really need to do it.

"That said, it is easy to make mistakes like that, we know that at a track like this. But you are in a Mercedes that was clearly in a league of his own at this track, first lap of Q1, you didn't need to take that much risk.

"It just caught him out, the grip that he clearly had at Turn One. He turned in, you go into qualifying and the car is always a bit more alive I guess than it would have been for him in FP3 and it has caught him out."
Russell 'can't discount' Antonelli from battle for win
Saturday's race comes just three weeks on from Antonelli's stunning victory at the Italian Grand Prix, which saw him come from 19th on the grid to win his home race.
Russell, who started second in Monza and led before being overhauled by Antonelli, is wary of the threat his team-mate could pose from towards the back of the grid in Baku.
"Obviously, you can't discount Kimi," Russell said. "He started 19th in Monza and now he's in 16th, so he should be leading by a few laps earlier this time."
Russell was asked whether he thought Antonelli was experiencing "jitters" as he nears a fist title, but pointed out that even in championship-winning campaigns, drivers tend to make mistakes.
Sky Sports F1's Karun Chandhok is joined by George Russell to watch back his pole-setting lap for the Azerbaijan GP
The Brit preferred to focus on his own strong performance so far in Baku, which had seen him appear to have an edge over Antonelli even before the Q1 crash.
"I can't recall many mistakes he's made this season," Russell said. "The performance our side today was great, but he's been flawless this whole season.
"When you look at every championship campaign, even for the winners, there are mistakes along the way.

"I still keep on believing and keep on fighting until it isn't possible anymore, but I don't feel any pressure. I feel excitement every time I jump in the car now, purely because I feel more confident in myself.

"When that confidence starts to build, it's just like this upward cycle. And on the flip side, when you're on the back foot, you start losing that confidence, and then you start pushing the limits more, and that's when mistakes happen.
